solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Irritable declaration of one in Casualty?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: short-tempered, unwilling to wait
second meaning, read as two words: ..., what someone being treated in a hospital's casualty department might announce

explanation.walkthrough: Casualty is the British name for a hospital's accident and emergency department; split the answer after its third letter to hear a patient introducing themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless and quick to anger at delay is said to be lacking patience, the adjective's ordinary sense.

clue.text: Suffer among reactionary force of old

parts.note: among means in

indicators.note: something reactionary turns back, so the force's letters run backwards in this down light

parts.note: the RUC, Royal Ulster Constabulary, a police force replaced in 2001

explanation.surface: A complaint about being treated badly by a reactionary police force of times past.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001, hence 'of old'.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to suffer or bring it upon oneself.

clue.text: Sarcastic chap cracking jokes?

parts.note: a pun is a joke that someone cracks
a chap is a gent

explanation.surface: Describing a wisecracking man whose humour has a cutting edge.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as PUN GENT: a gentleman who cracks puns.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent remarks are sharp and biting, close to sarcastic or caustic in tone.

clue.text: Pioneer's guard dog crossing river

indicators.note: the guard word spans the river abbreviation, holding it within

parts.note: to guard is to tend or look after
R is the map abbreviation for river
a setter is a gundog breed

explanation.surface: A pioneering guard dog makes its way across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Pioneer stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A trendsetter leads where others follow, an innovator starting a fashion before the crowd.

clue.text: Last two avoiding service still

indicators.note: the final pair of letters keeps away from the word, so its last two letters are dropped

parts.note: evensong is the evening church service

explanation.surface: Instructions about skipping the end of a church service, yet still attending.
explanation.walkthrough: Evensong is the Anglican evening service; lose NG, its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so is an adverbial phrase meaning nevertheless, the concessive sense of still.

clue.text: Everything in factory?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a works is a factory

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the stretch of reading 'in factory' as being in the works.
explanation.definitionFit: The works is an informal idiom for all of something, every possible extra included.

clue.text: Peg wants to succeed for the most part

indicators.note: only most of the phrase is used, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: to succeed is to do well

explanation.surface: Someone called Peg is ambitious and mostly hopes to prosper.
explanation.walkthrough: Peg looks like a woman's name, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a wooden pin or rod used to join pieces of timber.

clue.text: Stretcher bearer going the wrong way? What an idiot!

indicators.note: travelling the wrong way means the bearer's letters run upwards in this down light

parts.note: a stretcher is a brick laid lengthwise, and a hod is what carries bricks

explanation.surface: An ambulance stretcher-bearer heads off in the wrong direction, and someone exclaims at his folly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretcher bearer' suggests ambulance work; a stretcher is a brick laid lengthwise in a wall, and the builder's hod carries bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Doh is the exclamation, popularised by Homer Simpson, made on realising a foolish blunder.

clue.text: Ravenous and unhappy, knocked up some food

indicators.note: knocked upwards, so in this down light the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: low means unhappy or depressed
fish is one kind of food

explanation.surface: A hungry, miserable cook throws together a quick meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfish hunger is fierce and greedy, as a wolf's is supposed to be.

clue.text: Duke learning about city once besieged

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman studies the history of a city that endured a siege.
explanation.walkthrough: Leningrad, now St Petersburg again, endured a siege of almost 900 days in World War II.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the Soviet name of the Russian city blockaded by German forces from 1941 to 1944.

clue.text: Meet clergyman eating ice cream? On the contrary

indicators.note: eating suggests one thing taking another into itself
this reverses the stated roles, so the ice cream holds the clergyman instead

parts.note: a cone is an ice cream served in a wafer cone
VEN abbreviates Venerable, the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: An invitation to meet a churchman who is enjoying an ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a vicar licking an ice; 'On the contrary' reverses who eats whom, so the ice cream holds the churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: To convene is to assemble or gather together, as a committee does when it sits.

clue.text: Time to embrace revolutionary left's rank

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so the time word wraps the other letters

parts.note: an eon is a vast period of time
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: Time for an embrace of the left wing's ranks by a revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a level or grade in an organisation, as in the upper echelons of power.

clue.text: Regret abusive Democrat must be removed

indicators.note: the named party has to go, so its letter is taken out

parts.note: rude means abusive or insulting
D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: A political party regrets an abusive member who must be expelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to wish it had not happened, a literary verb for repenting.

clue.text: Bent copper facing end of his employment

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector, a police officer

indicators.note: end picks just the final letter of the following word

parts.note: a position is a job or employment

explanation.surface: A corrupt policeman is about to lose his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent copper' reads as British slang for a corrupt police officer, but Bent is the definition and 'copper' gives DI.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent for something is a natural inclination or temperament, which is what disposition means.

clue.text: Meet painter, remarkably self-indulgent

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something done in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist one meets turns out to be remarkably given to excess.
explanation.definitionFit: Intemperate people lack moderation and restraint, especially with drink, giving in to their appetites.

clue.text: Saw for example Conservative leading state

indicators.note: the party letter goes first, ahead of the other part

parts.note: to utter is to state or say

explanation.surface: A Conservative heading a state, seen for example as leading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' could be the past tense of see; here it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is one kind of blade-based tool for cutting through material.

clue.text: Best days for one in minority?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the period often looked back on as the happiest of one's life
second meaning: a minor, legally under age, is in the time of life before adulthood

explanation.walkthrough: 'Minority' suggests a group outnumbered; legally it is the state of being under age.
explanation.definitionFit: Early years before adulthood are commonly idealised as the happiest time of life.

clue.text: One drawing is of Her Majesty on small boat

indicators.note: in an across light, placed on means coming after

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A portrait of the Queen aboard a little vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketcher is an artist who makes rough drawings, so one drawing describes them.

clue.text: Uncle's place, where you can get dubious material, I hear

indicators.note: what I hear signals a sound-alike word

parts.words: where you can get dubious material
parts.note: a porn shop sells dubious material; in a non-rhotic accent it sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: Someone's uncle runs a shop with suspect merchandise, or so they hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, who lends money against pledged goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawnbroker's premises is where goods are pledged for loans; uncle is old slang for that trade.

clue.text: He perhaps is in Tangiers working

indicators.note: working implies the letters are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is employed in Tangiers, in Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the chemical symbol for helium, not a pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium is an example of the noble elements that hardly react with anything.

clue.text: Left without Charlie, on a high

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the departure word goes around the letter

parts.note: exited means left, went out
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone went off without their friend, while elated or intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense outside, so C goes inside EXITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a high is feeling elated and thrilled, a state of agitation and eagerness.

clue.text: Threaten island legislator with death

parts.note: an MP, Member of Parliament, makes laws
one's end is one's death

explanation.surface: An island politician is threatened with death.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that impends hangs over us, looming and about to happen menacingly.

clue.text: Question old flame, an explosive type?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
an indefinite article gives A
a mine is a kind of explosive device

explanation.surface: Questioning a former lover with an explosive temper.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'explosive type' sounds like a hot-tempered person; here it is a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine a witness is to question them, as in cross-examination.

clue.text: Talk foolishly about current danger on the seas

indicators.note: about here means around, so the talk word surrounds the current letter

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly at length
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone chatters idly about the risks of a current at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is a sea robber, a menace to ships and sailors.

clue.text: Opinionated idiot can err horribly

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An opinionated fool is capable of making terrible mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrinaire person applies theory rigidly and dogmatically, unwilling to consider other views.

clue.text: Soldiers moving south for dope

indicators.note: south is downward, the bottom or end, so the first letter goes to the back

parts.note: the SAS, the British Special Air Service

explanation.surface: Troops heading south in search of drugs or information.
explanation.walkthrough: SAS is the British army's Special Air Service; its first S moves to the end. 'Dope' looks like drugs but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a fool, and calling someone an ass says the same thing.

clue.text: Time for a bit of magic

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an incantation or charm

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a magician's cue; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a stretch of duration and an enchantment cast by a witch.

clue.text: Nothing unreasonable about way one refuses to face reality

indicators.note: about here means next to, so the two parts sit side by side

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
rich, as in 'that's rich', means unreasonable or outrageous

explanation.surface: Someone avoids anything unreasonable on their path and refuses to face facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's rich!' is said of an unreasonable or outrageous claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostriches supposedly bury their heads in sand, so the bird names a person in denial.

clue.text: Cockney's rent causing outrage?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: to hire is to rent

explanation.surface: A Londoner's rent increase causing anger.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is anger or wrath, and outrage is strong indignant anger.

clue.text: Greed, a weakness holding soldiers back

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the weakness wraps the soldiers

parts.note: a vice is a moral weakness

indicators.note: back means the soldiers' letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Greed described as a failing that holds soldiers back.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an extreme desire for wealth, one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Subterfuge of old magistrate, jailing Penny once

indicators.note: jailing means locking up inside, so the magistrate holds the coin

parts.note: a doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa
D was the abbreviation for an old penny, before decimalisation

explanation.surface: A trick played by a former judge in locking up a woman named Penny.
explanation.walkthrough: D, from Latin denarius, was the old British penny before 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a trick or ruse, a crafty way of evading something.

clue.text: Bit by bit story spread

parts.note: a piece is an article or story in a newspaper
a spread is a large meal laid out

explanation.surface: A tale spread around a little at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Done piecemeal means done gradually, in stages rather than all at once.
